name: Prose scene

beats.name: Want
beats.ask: What does somebody in this scene want, in this scene, concretely?

beats.name: Obstacle
beats.ask: What is between them and it — and is it a person?

beats.name: Turn
beats.ask: What changes? A scene where nothing changes is a description.

beats.name: Cost
beats.ask: What did it cost, and who pays later?

note: No line rules. A scene is a unit of change: somebody wants something, something is in the way, the situation turns, and the turn costs. The four beats are not an outline to fill in — they are the four questions you can ask a finished draft to find out whether it is a scene or a passage.
ground: This is the working shape used across screenwriting and fiction craft alike, and it is descriptive rather than prescriptive: it names what scenes that work turn out to have.
ask: If you cut this scene, what in the next one stops making sense?
